chunks: And Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad and others narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Mūsā ibn ‘Umar, from Sāliḥ ibn Sindi Al-Jammāl, from a man from Ahl al-Raqqah, who was called Abū was called Abū al-Maḍā’, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me: ‘Do you go to the grave of Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him)?’ I said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Do you take provisions (sufur) for that?’ I said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘If you were going to the graves of your fathers and mothers, you would not do that.’ I said: ‘Then what should we eat?’ He said: ‘Bread and milk.’

And Karrām said to Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him): ‘May I be your ransom! Some people who visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) take tasty provisions.’ He said: ‘Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me: ‘If they were visiting the graves of their mothers and fathers, they would not do that.’

key_terms.الْخُبْزَ وَاللَّبَنَ: Bread and milk, representing simple, staple food.
key_terms.سُفْراً: Provisions or food taken on a journey, often implying a variety or abundance of food.
key_terms.قُبُورَ آبَائِكُمْ: The graves of your fathers, used here as a comparative reference for ordinary visits.
key_terms.يُطَيِّبُونَ: They make sweet/tasty, referring to preparing delicious or varied foods.

ai.seo_question: What kind of food should be taken when visiting the grave of Imam al-Husain (a.s.) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) uses the analogy of visiting one's parents to illustrate that the ziyārah of Imām al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is a solemn act of worship (ʿibādah) rather than a leisurely social excursion, hence the recommendation for simple provisions like bread and milk. This hadith, found in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyārah*, underscores the Shia emphasis on humility and spiritual focus during pilgrimage, distinguishing it from the cultural practice of treating graves as sites for festive gatherings.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad and others narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Mūsā ibn ‘Umar, from Sāliḥ ibn Sindi Al-Jammāl, from someone who was from Raqqah, whose name was Abul Maďā, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) asked me, “Do you go to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Ḥusain (a.s.))?” I replied, “Yes.” Imam (a.s.) asked, “Do you take different kinds of food with you?” I replied, “Yes.” Imam (a.s.) said, “Verily if you were going to the graves of your own fathers and mothers, you would not have done this.” I asked, “Then what should we eat?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Bread and milk.”

Abul Maďā (the narrator) added: Kirām (‘Abdul Karīm ibn ‘Amr Al-Khath’ami) narrated that he said to Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “May I sacrifice myself for you! Some people who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) take tasty foods with them.” Imam (a.s.) said, “Verily if they were going to the graves of their own fathers and mothers, they would not have done this.”
